sentences.text: This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.40,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 11-03-2023 at about 00.30 a.m., the petitioner was riding the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-02-HF-626 towards Akkinalu Village, on the extreme left side of Bengaluru-Tumkur NH-48 road, slowly and cautiously, by observing the traffic rules and regulations.

When he reached near Reliance Petrol Bunk, Binnamangala,
Nelamangala, Bengaluru District, the driver of lorry bearing Reg. No.MH-43-Y-2913,
had parked the said lorry on two- wheeler passing road, without switching on the indicator or taking safety measures, in the early morning.
Due to which the accident has occurred and the petitioner has fell down along with the motorcycle and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Manasvi Hospital, wherein he took conservative treatment and then he was shifted to Truelife Speciality Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as an in- patient.
Earlier to the accident, he was working in Blue Dart Courier and was earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
The Nelamangala Traffic Police have registered the case against the driver of the said lorry, for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 338 of IPC.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.

Hence,
they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

Therefore,
it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.40,00,000/- with interest.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondent No.2 has appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement.
Whereas, the respondent No.1 did not choose to appear and remained absent.

Hence, the respondent No.1 is placed as ex-parte.
4.
The respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.

It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of lorry bearing No.MH-43-Y-2913, vide policy bearing No.VGC0888574000100 in favour of respondent No.1 and it was valid from 10-01-2023 to 09-01-2024.
Further it is contended that, the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the insured vehicle as on the date of accident.

Further it is contended that, the petition is bad for non-compliance of provisions under Section 134(c) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.

Further it is contended that, no accident as stated in the claim petition has taken place, the lorry bearing Reg. No.MH- 43-Y-2913 was not at all involved in the alleged accident and the petitioner has not sustained any injuries in the alleged accident, as stated in the claim petition.
There is no nexus between injuries sustained to the petitioner and alleged accident.
The alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent riding on the part of the petitioner himself.
The petitioner has filed a false petition to get unlawful gain.
Further, it has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries sustained, medical expenses and treatment taken by him.

Further it is contended that, the lorry bearing Reg.
No.MH-43-Y-2913 was not possessing valid fitness certificate and permit to ply the said vehicle on the road.
As such, there is violation of terms and conditions of the policy and rules and regulations of Motor Vehicles Act.
Further, it has sought permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.1 under Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above stated denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident, alleged to have occurred on 11-03-2023 at about 00.30 a.m., due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg.
No.MH-43-Y-2913 ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3. What order or Award ?

Further, he has got examined two more witnesses namely Dr.
Shailesh A.V. Rao and Dr. Nagaraj B.N. as P.W.1 and P.W.3 respectively and closed his side.

On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has examined its representative/Legal Manager as R.W.1 and got marked 2 documents as Ex.R.1 and 2 and closed its side.
7.
I have heard the arguments of both the sides and perused the entire material placed on record.

sentences.text: Further, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner has remained undisputed by the owner of offending lorry/Respondent No.1, as he did not choose to appear and contest the case of the petitioner.

But, the respondent No.2 has specifically denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident and has taken specific defence that, the lorry bearing Reg.
No.MH-43-Y- 2913 was not at all involved in the alleged accident, the petitioner has not sustained any injuries in the alleged accident, as stated in the claim petition and there is no nexus between injuries sustained to the petitioner and alleged accident.
Further it is contended that, the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent riding on the part of the petitioner himself.
But, the respondent No.2 has failed to establish the said contentions.

Except the self serving statements of the R.W.1, who is the representative/Legal Manager of respondent No.2 insurance company, there is no other corroborative oral or documentary evidence placed on record by the respondent No.2 to show that, the alleged accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the petitioner himself and the lorry bearing Reg. No.MH-43-Y-2913 was not at all involved in the said accident.
The same could have been established by examining any independent eye-witness to the alleged accident.
But, the respondent No.2 has not taken any strain to summon and examine the eye-witness to the accident in question, for the reasons best known to it.

On the other hand, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, the said accident has taken place due to negligently parking of offending lorry bearing Reg.
No.MH-43-Y-2913 on the road by its driver, without switching on indicators and taking safety measures in the mid-night hours.

Due to which, the motorcycle of the petitioner got dashed against the rare portion of the offending lorry and thereby the petitioner fell down on the road and has sustained grievous injuries on his head and other parts of the body.

Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross- examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been brought out from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence or which establishes that, the said accident has not taken place solely due to rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle by the petitioner himself or there was any contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner in the cause of accident.

13. Further, the Ex.P.6 spot mahazar also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place on the left side of 26 feet wide on Bengaluru-Tumkur NH-48 road, near Reliance Petrol Bunk,
Binnamangala, Kasaba Hobli, Nelamangala Taluk, Bengaluru District, due to dashing of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-HF-0626 to the rare portion of lorry bearing Reg. No.MH-43-Y-2913,
which was parked on the road, at the distance of 6 feet from the edge of the road and 20 feet from the median divider wall of the road.
Further, as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.7, the accident is not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident.

When the accident was not caused due to the any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident and there was no negligence on the part of the petitioner/rider of the motorcycle, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to negligent act of the driver of offending vehicle.

Further, the investigation officer in his Ex.P.9 final report/charge-sheet has clearly stated that, the accident in question has taken place due to negligent act of the driver of offending lorry bearing Reg.

sentences.text: Admittedly, the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged either by the driver or the owner of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.MH-43-Y-2913.

In such circumstances,
there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident, negligence of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.

14. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.1 OPD records, Ex.P.2 neuro-psychological assessment report, Ex.P.3 mini mental state examination report, Ex.P.8 wound certificate, Ex.P.14 and 15 discharge summaries (total 2), Ex.P.21 lab report, Ex.P.22 letter issued by Manasvi Hospital,
Bengaluru, Ex.P.23 clinical notes and Ex.P.24 x-ray, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in a road traffic accident.

The petitioner has sustained head injury,
C4-C5 vertebral body undisplaced fracture, multiple facial bone fracture, lung contusion and left patella fracture, left lateral malleolus fracture and right volar barton fracture.
The same is deposed by P.W.1 and P.W.3, who are the doctors who have clinically examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability.
On the other hand, there is no rebuttal evidence produced by the respondent No.2, to show that the above medical records are false documents.
There is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.

Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can safely be held that,
the respondent No.2 has failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending lorry bearing Reg.
No.MH-43-Y-2913 and injuries sustained to the petitioner in the said accident.

15. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

sentences.text:
The medical records placed on record clearly speaks that, the petitioner has sustained head injury, C4-C5 vertebral body undisplaced fracture, multiple facial bone fracture,
lung contusion and left patella fracture, left lateral malleolus fracture and right volar barton fracture and for the said injuries he has undergone surgery.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport,
actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non-pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
i) Towards loss of future income:
In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.
To prove his age, the petitioner has produced the notarised copy of his Aadhar card and PAN card, which are marked as Ex.P.10 and 11.
As per Ex.P.10 and 11, the date of birth of the petitioner is 18-07-1994.
The accident has taken place on 11-03-2023 at about 00:30 a.m.
This clearly goes to show that, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident was 29 years.

Further, the P.W.1, who is the doctor who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability,
has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has suffered head injury, C4-C5 vertebral body undisplaced fracture, multiple facial bone fracture, lung contusion and left patella fracture, left lateral malleolus fracture and right volar barton fracture.
Further he has deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries suffered by the petitioner he found that, there is 70% physical disability to the whole body of the petitioner.

Further, the Ex.P.1 OPD records, Ex.P.2 neuro-psychological assessment report, Ex.P.3 mini mental state examination report, Ex.P.8 wound certificate,
Ex.P.14 and 15 discharge summaries (total 2), Ex.P.21 lab report, Ex.P.22 letter issued by Manasvi Hospital, Bengaluru clearly speaks that, the petitioner has suffered the above stated injuries and he has undergone surgery for the said injuries.

Though,
the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.

Further, he has clearly denied the suggestions made to him that, the petitioner has not suffered any disability as stated his affidavit and in order to help the petitioner to claim more compensation he has exaggerated the percentage of disability.

The P.W.1 has deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, the accident has occurred on 11-03-2023 and he has assessed the disability to the petitioner on 06-01- 2024, which is after lapse of twelve months from the date of injuries caused to the petitioner.

Further, the P.W.1 has clearly admitted in his cross-examination that, he has not produced the manual to show that the 70% disability is prescribed for the categories of the injuries mentioned in the wound certificate.

Further, he has clearly admitted that, he has not gone through the case-sheet of the petitioner before assessing the disability and he has not produced the disability certificate Chethan Kumar S.R vs Nizam Bechan Khan on 1 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141470471/
7 issued by the General Hospital, Ramanagar.

sentences.text: Further, he has clearly admitted that, he has not produced the MRI films and reports to the Court.
Further, he has clearly admitted that, in the discharge summary of Manasvi Hospital only one injury i.e. fracture of left mandible is stated.

But,
he denies that, the petitioner has not sustained any internal brain injury.

Further, the P.W.3, who is the doctor who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability in respect of orthopaedic injuries, has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has suffered head injury, C4- C5 vertebral body undisplaced fracture, multiple facial bone fracture, lung contusion and left patella fracture, left lateral malleolus fracture and right volar barton fracture.

Further he has deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries suffered by the petitioner he found that, there is 40%
physical disability of left lower limb, 35% physical disability of right upper limb and 24% physical disability to the whole body of the petitioner.

Further, the Ex.P.8 wound certificate, Ex.P.14 and 15 discharge summaries (total 2), Ex.P.21 lab report, Ex.P.22 letter issued by Manasvi Hospital,
Bengaluru, Ex.P.23 clinical notes and Ex.P.24 x-ray clearly speaks that, the petitioner has suffered the above stated injuries and he has undergone surgery for the said injuries.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.3 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.
Further, he has clearly denied the suggestions made to him that, the petitioner has not suffered any disability and he has exaggerated the percentage of disability.
But, the P.W.3 has deposed that, the petitioner needs to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants.
This clearly goes to show that, the disability has been assessed before completion of full treatment to the petitioner.
As per the gazette notification issued by the Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India, the disability should be assessed after completion of treatment.

sentences.text:
If the disability had been assessed after removal of all implants,
perhaps there would have been reduction in the percentage of the disability.

Further it is pertinent to note that, P.W.3 has clearly admitted in his cross-examination that, the fractures are united with implants in situ, the stability and mobility components of hip and ankle are normal, the petitioner can walk without any difficulties and external support, the petitioner can perform his day to day activities with some difficulties and he has not assessed the neuro-psychological disability of the petitioner.
As per P.W.1 the petitioner had impaired memory and intelligence.
He has suffered motor disability of right side, speech disability and cognitive disability.
It is pertinent to note that,
the P.W.1 has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessing the neurological disability on 06-01-2024 and 09-01-2024 i.e. approximately 2 year back.
There are every chances of some improvement in his mental health condition of the petitioner and reduction of disability as on today.

Therefore, in such circumstances and taking into consideration the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, avocation of the petitioner, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence available on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the disability of 50% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
a) The petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, before accident he was working in Blue Dart Courier and was earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.
Further, he has deposed that, due to grievous injuries suffered in the said accident he is unable to do his work.
The respondent No.2 has specifically denied the same.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.

To substantiate the same, the petitioner has produced company identity card,
appointment letter and pay slips (total 5), which are marked as Ex.P.16 to 18.

As per the said Chethan Kumar S.R vs Nizam Bechan Khan on 1 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141470471/
8 documents, the petitioner was drawing gross salary of Rs.20,346/-.

sentences.text: After deducting professional tax of Rs.200/-, the net salary of the petitioner comes to Rs.20,146/-.
Therefore, it is held that, as on the date of accident the monthly income of the petitioner was Rs.20,146/- per month.
Accordingly, the annual income of the petitioner is held at Rs.2,41,752/-.

b) As per the ratio laid down in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, the appropriate multiplier for a person whose is aged about 29 years is 17.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298

sentences.text: Therefore, loss of future income is Total annual income X disability/100 X multiplier = Rs.2,41,752 X 50/100 X 17 = Rs.20,54,892/-.
ii) Medical expenses:

The petitioner has deposed that, he has incurred expenses of Rs.16,00,000/-
towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charge etc.
In order to prove the same, he has produced 143 medical bills, as per Ex.P.19.
All the bills have been examined carefully and found that the petitioner has spent total amount of Rs.15,96,817/- towards medical expenses.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.15,96,817/- under the head of medical expenses.
iii) Pain and sufferings:

In the present case, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries i.e. head injury, C4-C5 vertebral body undisplaced fracture, multiple facial bone fracture, lung contusion and left patella fracture, left lateral malleolus fracture and right volar barton fracture.
As per Ex.P.14 and 15 discharge summary (total 2)

, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 84 days from 12-03-2023 to 27-03-2023 and 27-03-2023 to 03-06- 2023, in True Life Speciality Hospital,
Bengaluru.
Further, as per P.W.2, the said injuries have caused physical disability to the petitioner.
In such circumstances, certainly the petitioner would have suffered pain and sufferings.

Therefore,
taking into considering the injuries sustained and disability to the petitioner, this Court is of the opinion that, an compensation amount of Rs.1,00,000/- is to be awarded to the petitioner towards pain and sufferings.
iv) Attendant charges:
As per Ex.P.14 and 15 discharge summary (total 2), the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 84 days in True Life Speciality Hospital, Bengaluru.
He might have spent considerable amount towards attendant charges during that period.
Therefore, compensation of Rs.1000 x 84 = Rs.84,000/- is awarded towards the attendant charges.
v) Food and nourishment:
As per Ex.P.14 and 15 discharge summary (total 2), the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 84 days in True Life Speciality Hospital, Bengaluru.
He might have spent considerable amount towards food and nourishment during that period.

Therefore,
compensation of Rs.800 x 84 = Rs.67,200/- is awarded towards food and nourishment charges.
vi) Conveyance expenses:

The petitioner is the resident of Suthallipalya, Hakkinalu, Magadi Taluk,
Ramanagara, the accident has occurred on Bengaluru- Tumkur NH-48 road, near Reliance Petrol Bunk, Binnamangala, Kasaba Hobli, Nelamangala Taluk, Bengaluru District and he has taken treatment at True Life Speciality Hospital, Bengaluru.
Taking into consideration the distance in between the above places, compensation of Rs.20,000/- is awarded towards conveyance.

Therefore,
Rs.20,146/- x 10 = Rs.2,01,460/- is awarded towards loss of income during treatment period.
viii) Loss of amenities:

It is evident from the documents placed on record that, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 29 years and unfortunately he has suffered head injury, C4-C5 vertebral body undisplaced fracture, multiple facial bone fracture, lung contusion and left patella fracture, left lateral malleolus fracture and right volar barton fracture.
Further, he has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 50% to the whole body.
Therefore, awarding compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- towards loss of amenities would be just and reasonable.
ix) Future medical expenses:
The P.W.3 has clearly deposed in his evidence that, the petitioner needs to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants, the estimate of this surgery is around Rs.90,000/-.
But, admittedly the P.W.3 has not issued estimation of cost for the said surgery.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards future medical expenses would be just and reasonable.

19. Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads as follows:
1. Loss of future income Rs. 20,54,892-00 2.
Medical expenses 15,96,817-00 3. Pain and sufferings 1,00,000-00 4.
Attendant charges 84,000-00 5.

Conveyance expenses 20,000-00 7. Loss of income during 2,01,460-00 treatment period 8. Loss of amenities 1,00,000-00
9. Future medical expenses 20,000-00 Total Rs.42,44,369-00

In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.42,44,369/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.MH-43-Y-2913 the accident in question has taken place.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the said vehicle.

ORDER
The petition is partly allowed with costs.

opennyai_summary.facts:
This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.40,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.
Due to which the accident has occurred and the petitioner has fell down along with the motorcycle and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
Earlier to the accident, he was working in Blue Dart Courier and was earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
The Nelamangala Traffic Police have registered the case against the driver of the said lorry, for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 338 of IPC.
Hence,
they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

Further it is contended that, the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent riding on the part of the petitioner himself.
Except the self serving statements of the R.W.1, who is the representative/Legal Manager of respondent No.2 insurance company, there is no other corroborative oral or documentary evidence placed on record by the respondent No.2 to show that, the alleged accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the petitioner himself and the lorry bearing Reg. No.MH-43-Y-2913 was not at all involved in the said accident.
The same could have been established by examining any independent eye-witness to the alleged accident.
When the accident was not caused due to the any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident and there was no negligence on the part of the petitioner/rider of the motorcycle, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to negligent act of the driver of offending vehicle.
Further, the investigation officer in his Ex.P.9 final report/charge-sheet has clearly stated that, the accident in question has taken place due to negligent act of the driver of offending lorry bearing Reg.
On the other hand, there is no rebuttal evidence produced by the respondent No.2, to show that the above medical records are false documents.
There is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.
Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can safely be held that,
the respondent No.2 has failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending lorry bearing Reg.

15. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."
The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport,
actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non-pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
i) Towards loss of future income:
In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.
Therefore, in such circumstances and taking into consideration the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, avocation of the petitioner, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence available on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the disability of 50% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.
